summary: Registering a Shopify public OAuth app requires creating a Partner account, configuring API access scopes, and building mandatory GDPR webhook endpoints. While credentials are generated immediately for testing on development stores, public listing and multi-store deployment require passing a manual Shopify App Review process.

difficulty.headline: Public apps must adhere to strict platform requirements, implement mandatory billing/GDPR endpoints, and pass a manual review process that has a backlogged queue.

factors.label: Strict App Review & Queue Penalties
factors.detail: App submissions are manually reviewed against platform guidelines, and fixing rejections sends your app back to the end of the review queue.

evidence.quote: Every submission goes through the same review process, and our team is working through the backlog.

factors.label: Mandatory Compliance Endpoints
factors.detail: All public apps must implement and expose functional GDPR mandatory webhooks (customer data request, customer data erasure, and shop data erasure).

evidence.quote: Shopify requires all public apps to handle GDPR compliance webhooks.

factors.label: Session Token Requirements
factors.detail: Embedded apps must use session tokens instead of relying on third-party cookies or local storage.

evidence.quote: Your embedded app must function properly without relying on third-party cookies or local storage, including when accessed in incognito mode on Chrome.

can_test_before_approval.detail: Developers can immediately obtain API credentials upon creating an app and install it on development stores to build and test functionality before submitting for review.

evidence.quote: Development stores can be used to test apps to ensure they're free of bugs or otherwise incomplete.

requirements.label: Shopify Partner Account
requirements.detail: A free Shopify Partner account is required to access the Dev Dashboard and register OAuth apps.

evidence.quote: All new apps must be created via the Shopify Dev Dashboard or Partner Dashboard.

requirements.label: Development Store
requirements.detail: A development store under your Partner account is needed to test app installation, OAuth flow, and functionality.

evidence.quote: Development stores can be used to test apps to ensure they're free of bugs or otherwise incomplete.

requirements.label: GDPR Compliance Webhook Endpoints
requirements.detail: Public endpoints to receive customer data request, customer data erasure, and shop data erasure notifications.

evidence.quote: Shopify requires all public apps to handle GDPR compliance webhooks.

requirements.label: HTTPS Redirection URL
requirements.detail: A secure callback URI to receive OAuth authorization codes during authentication.

steps.title: Create a Shopify Partner Account
steps.detail: Sign up for a free Shopify Partner account to access the Dev Dashboard where app registrations are managed.

evidence.quote: All new apps must be created via the Shopify Dev Dashboard or Partner Dashboard.

steps.title: Create a Development Store
steps.detail: Set up a development store within your Partner account to serve as a sandbox environment for testing installation and API calls.

evidence.quote: Development stores can be used to test apps to ensure they're free of bugs or otherwise incomplete.

steps.title: Register App & Obtain Credentials
steps.detail: Create a new app entry in the Dev Dashboard to generate the Client ID (SHOPIFY_API_KEY) and Client Secret (SHOPIFY_API_SECRET).
steps.agent_assist: Draft the app configuration options, app name (avoiding restricted terms like 'Shopify'), and specify the App URL and callback redirection URIs.

evidence.quote: Your app's client credentials consist of a client ID and a client secret.

steps.title: Configure Scopes and GDPR Webhooks
steps.detail: Declare necessary API access scopes and configure mandatory GDPR webhook URLs (customer data request, customer data erasure, shop data erasure).
steps.agent_assist: Prepare the minimum required scope list (e.g. read_products, read_orders) with justifications, and generate configuration for GDPR endpoints.

evidence.quote: Request only the data your app needs to function.

steps.title: Test OAuth Flow & App Lifecycle on Dev Store
steps.detail: Install the app on your development store. Test the full OAuth authorization code flow, session token validation, and uninstall/reinstall routines.
steps.agent_assist: Draft a comprehensive testing checklist covering installation, re-authentication, billing flow, and webhook handling.

evidence.quote: Make sure you thoroughly test installing, uninstalling, and reinstalling your app, as this tripped us up several times.

steps.title: Draft Listing Page and Review Submissions
steps.detail: Prepare the public app listing content, key benefit summaries, app screenshots, demo store details, and testing instructions for the review team.
steps.agent_assist: Draft app listing copy (tagline, key benefits, feature descriptions), reviewer instructions, and screencast scripts.

evidence.quote: The app listing page is technically your only sales pitch to the merchant.

steps.title: Submit App for Review
steps.detail: Submit the completed app configuration, listing form, and test instructions in the Partner Dashboard for Shopify App Review.
steps.agent_assist: Provide a pre-submission verification checklist ensuring all requirements, test credentials, and billing rules are satisfied.

evidence.quote: The app review team will only review production-ready apps.

steps.title: Provider App Review
steps.detail: Shopify's App Review team evaluates your app submission against platform quality standards. Note: review times vary depending on backlog (no official figure provided).

evidence.quote: Every submission goes through the same review process, and our team is working through the backlog.

steps.title: Publish App to Shopify App Store
steps.detail: Once approved by the review team, approve the final listing version and publish your app to make it available to merchants.

gotchas.title: Resubmission Resets Review Queue Position
gotchas.detail: If your app is rejected during review, submitting a fix places your app at the back of the queue, significantly increasing overall wait time.

evidence.quote: Every submission goes through the same review process, and our team is working through the backlog.

gotchas.title: 60-Day Historical Order Window Restriction
gotchas.detail: By default, order access scopes only grant data for the last 60 days. Requesting historical data requires approval for the read_all_orders scope.

gotchas.title: Repeated Failures Risk Suspension
gotchas.detail: Submitting apps with unresolved bugs repeatedly can result in temporary partner account suspension.

evidence.quote: Apps that repeatedly fail review may be subject to a temporary suspension.

gotchas.title: Exposing Client Secret in Client-Side Code
gotchas.detail: The Client Secret must remain strictly server-side and should never be committed to version control or included in frontend client bundles.

evidence.quote: Never commit credentials to version control.

blockers.problem: App URL fails to redirect to OAuth grant screen upon installation
blockers.why: Shopify requires both the main App URL and allowed redirection URLs to seamlessly direct merchants to the OAuth consent page.
blockers.fix: Verify that your application handles unauthenticated requests by initiating the OAuth flow and directing to Shopify's authorization URL.

blockers.problem: Rejection due to non-compliant billing integration
blockers.why: Shopify requires all paid public apps or apps with charges to process payments via the Shopify Billing API or managed pricing.
blockers.fix: Integrate Shopify's Billing API for all app subscription and usage charges rather than external payment processors.

blockers.problem: Reviewer unable to test features or access external accounts
blockers.why: The review team requires valid test credentials and setup instructions to fully verify app functionality.
blockers.fix: Provide working login credentials and step-by-step testing instructions in the submission notes.

uncertain: Exact SLA or calendar wait time for the Shopify App Review queue (sources note active backlogs and delays without a guaranteed timeframe).
Specific wait times for obtaining approval for protected customer data scopes.
